newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle end up ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle end up ahead of report.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed mostly higher on short covering and evening of positions ahead of Friday's USDA cattle data, traders said.

Renewed concern over wet, cold weather in the Plains over the weekend added to light position squaring early, but liquidation pared December gains. Bull spreading added to strength in February which becomes the lead month on Tuesday and carries a fairly large discount to cash, they said.
Spreaders bought February and sold April early on anticipation the report will show larger fed cattle supplies by the spring, pit sources said.

Estimates on the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report for feedlots of 1,000 head or more in the seven key states averaged 103.2 percent of last year for on-feed numbers as of December 1, in a range of 102 to 104.2 percent. Estimates on November placements averaged 105 percent in a range of 98 to 110 percent and marketings averaged 93.9 percent in a range of 91 to 98 percent of last year.
The heavy placements, if borne out by the report, would likely come to market in the spring, traders added.
In live cattle options, Shatkin bought next year December 72 to 76 calls early, pit sources said.

Trading was light in the feeder cattle pit early on mostly position-evening activity ahead of the report, but prices firmed along with gains in live cattle futures. Feeders will likely take cues from live cattle and grain markets the next couple of weeks as many feeder cattle auctions will be closed for the holidays, traders said.
ADM Investor Services notably sold March early. In options trade, LIT division of First Options bought August 68 calls and sold 72 calls, pit sources said.

Live cattle closed 0.075 cent per lb lower to 0.225 higher with only December off and February up 0.175 at 63.575 cents. Feeders ended up 0.025 to 0.250 cent with January up 0.150 at 65.900 cents. Distant December live cattle posted a new contract high in thin trade as did August, September and November feeder cattle contracts.
